note: Two experiments on one Windows PC. Experiment A = same code, four verdicts (default settings). Experiment B = speed on a 2000-module / 70,012-line synthetic clean codebase. Numbers are a 2026-06-30 snapshot; ty/pyrefly versions have since moved (monthly cadence). The structural findings are the durable claims, not exact seconds.

experiment_a_verdicts.description: 6 fixtures, four checkers, ALL default settings. Cell = errors reported.

rows.mypy: 0 (+note: bodies of untyped functions not checked)

experiment_b_speed.description: Synthetic codebase: 2000 modules, 70,012 lines, all type-clean. cold = first run, warm = immediate re-run. Median of 3. Wall time.

rows.note: First run builds .mypy_cache; warm (incremental) is Rust-class.
CLI has no incremental cache; ~1-2s node startup included every run.

ratios.desc: Rust tools ~15-30x faster COLD. mypy warm (0.27s) is Rust-class — its 'slow' reputation is mostly the cold path, which CI usually hits.

findings.claim: An unannotated parameter makes all four checkers skip a plain body bug; only mypy tells you it skipped.
findings.detail: def parse(raw): with raw.upper() assigned to an int passes ALL FOUR at default. Unannotated param = Unknown/Any -> body uncheckable. mypy emits 'By default the bodies of untyped functions are not checked, consider using --check-untyped-defs'. The other three are silent. Adding raw: str -> int makes ALL FOUR immediately flag the bug — proof that checker silence means 'you gave me nothing to check', not 'the code is correct'.

findings.claim: mypy widens reveal_type; the other three preserve Literal.
findings.detail: reveal_type((1, 'two')) -> mypy 2.1 shows tuple[int, str] (widened); pyright + the two Rust tools show tuple[Literal[1], Literal['two']].

findings.claim: pyrefly/ty flag reveal_type used without import; mypy/pyright stay silent.
findings.detail: A bare reveal_type(...) not imported from typing draws a runtime-failure diagnostic from pyrefly and ty; mypy and pyright treat it as special-form and say nothing.

findings.claim: pyright without a pinned venv treats PEP 695 'type X = ...' as requiring 3.12+.
findings.detail: Runs at a conservative default target version; adding pythonVersion 3.13 to pyrightconfig.json removes the warning. Environment not stated => conservative default.

findings.claim: pyrefly with no config runs to '0 errors' + exit 0 WITHOUT actually checking.
findings.detail: pyrefly check <files> with no pyrefly.toml prints '0 errors' and exit 0, plus a 'Run pyrefly init' hint — it did not check. Config must exist before real checking starts. Broken code can look clean.

findings.claim: mypy 2.0's answer to speed is parallelism, not a Rust rewrite.
findings.detail: --num-workers N (8 workers ~5x). mypy chose to shrink the cold path rather than rewrite in Rust.

explicitly_not_verified.note: Typing-spec conformance ordering (pyright/Zuban > pyrefly >90% > mypy > ty) is cited from public conformance data, NOT measured by this run. Cited, not measured.

The speed bench is a uniform, shallow-typed synthetic codebase. Heavy generics/overloads/metaclasses load each tool differently; those were not measured. ty's speed is also partly unimplemented rules (beta) — discount accordingly.
